title: More than just accuracy: A pathway-level framework for implementing blood and digital biomarkers for Alzheimer’s disease care
title_zh: 不止准确性：实现血液与数字生物标志物在阿尔茨海默病护理中的通路级框架
abstract: Blood biomarkers are transforming Alzheimer's disease diagnostics by enabling a scalable, minimally invasive assessment of pathology. Food and Drug Administration clearances and European market certifications of different plasma tests mark a shift toward biological diagnosis in routine care. However, clinical implementation is not guided by diagnostic accuracy alone but will depend on improved patient-centered and pathway-level outcomes, including diagnostic confidence, the appropriate use of CSF and PET assessments, time to diagnosis, amyloid-targeting treatment eligibility assessment, and trial recruitment. Digital biomarkers may complement blood tests by providing repeated measures of cognition, speech, and mobility. Yet, their evidence base remains more heterogeneous regarding construct validity, supervision requirements, device dependence, adherence burden, cultural portability, interpretability, and regulatory classification. This review defines how combined blood-digital workflows could be evaluated beyond accuracy, including the context of use, downstream decisions, ethical aspects, governance, and post-market monitoring, ultimately aiming to translate biomarker innovation into meaningful benefits for patients and health systems.
abstract_zh: 血液生物标志物正通过实现可扩展、微创的病理评估，改变阿尔茨海默病的诊断方式。不同血浆检测的美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA）批准和欧洲市场认证标志着日常护理向生物学诊断转变的进程。然而，临床实施并非仅由诊断准确性决定，而将取决于更好的以患者为中心和通路级结果，包括诊断信心、脑脊液（CSF）和正电子发射断层扫描（PET）评估的适当使用、诊断时间、针对淀粉样蛋白的治疗适应性评估以及试验招募。数字生物标志物可通过提供认知、语言和运动的重复测量来补充血液检测。然而，其证据基础在构念效度、监督需求、设备依赖、依从性负担、文化可迁移性、可解释性和监管分类等方面仍更为异质。本文综述了如何在准确性之外评估血液-数字工作流程，包括使用情境、下游决策、伦理方面、治理和上市后监测，最终旨在将生物标志物创新转化为对患者和卫生系统的有意义收益。
